questions.stem: A class has 28 students. 3/7 of them walk to school and 1/4 of them come by bus. The rest come by car. How many come by car?
questions.explanation: 3/7 of 28: 28 ÷ 7 = 4, × 3 = 12 walk. 1/4 of 28 = 7 by bus. 12 + 7 = 19 walk or bus, so 28 − 19 = 9 come by car.

distractors.E: walkers + bus, forgot to subtract from 28

questions.stem: Which number leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 3, and also leaves a remainder of 2 when divided by 4?
questions.explanation: Check each: 10 ÷ 3 rem 1 ✗. 17 ÷ 4 rem 1 ✗. 26 ÷ 3 = 8 rem 2 ✓ and 26 ÷ 4 = 6 rem 2 ✓. 30 ÷ 3 rem 0 ✗. 35 ÷ 4 rem 3 ✗. Shortcut: 2 more than a multiple of 12 (24 + 2).

questions.skill: Comparing fractions, fraction of an amount
questions.stem:
Which of these statements are correct?
1) 3/5 is greater than 5/8
2) 7/9 is closer to 1 than 6/7 is
3) 2/3 of 45 is the same as 3/5 of 50

distractors.A: compared numerators/denominators instead of real size
distractors.C: thinks bigger numbers in a fraction mean bigger fraction
distractors.D: judged closeness by the size of the denominator

questions.stem: Five friends read these numbers of books last term: Ana 4, Ben 7, Cai 3, Dev 6, Eli 5. Their average (mean) is 5 books. Fay joins the group, and now the average of all six is 6 books. How many books did Fay read?
questions.explanation: Average × number of people = total. Five friends: total 25. Six friends at an average of 6: total 36. Fay = 36 − 25 = 11.

questions.skill: Turns in degrees and compass directions
questions.stem: A robot faces north-east. It turns 135° clockwise, then 270° anticlockwise. Which way is it facing now?
questions.explanation: North-east → turn 135° clockwise (90° + 45°) → South. From South, 270° anticlockwise is the same as 90° clockwise → West.

distractors.B: added the turns and took off 360°

questions.stem: Juice is sold in three sizes: 250 mL for $1.20, 1 L for $4.20, and 2 L for $8.80. Mia needs exactly 3 litres and wants to spend as little as possible. How much does she pay?
questions.explanation: Cost per litre: 250 mL bottles $4.80, 1 L $4.20, 2 L $4.40. The 1 L bottle is cheapest per litre, so 3 × $4.20 = $12.60. The biggest bottle is not always the best deal!

distractors.C: assumed the biggest bottle is best (2 L + 1 L)

questions.stem: A number line goes from 2.4 to 2.6 and is split into 10 equal parts. An arrow points to the 7th mark after 2.4. What number does the arrow show?
questions.explanation: The gap is 2.6 − 2.4 = 0.2. Split into 10 parts, each part is 0.02. 7 parts = 0.14. 2.4 + 0.14 = 2.54.

distractors.E: thought each part is 0.1 (and ignored the end of the line)

questions.skill: Sharing in a ratio using parts
questions.stem: Sam and Lily share some stickers. For every 2 stickers Sam gets, Lily gets 3. Lily ends up with 18 more stickers than Sam. How many stickers are there altogether?
questions.explanation: Think in parts: Sam 2 parts, Lily 3 parts. Lily has 1 part more, and that is 18 stickers. Altogether 5 parts = 5 × 18 = 90 (Sam 36, Lily 54).

questions.stem: Ella has four digit cards: 1, 2, 3 and 4. She uses two different cards to make a 2-digit number. How many different EVEN numbers can she make?
questions.explanation: Even numbers end in 2 or 4. Ending in 2: 12, 32, 42 (3 numbers). Ending in 4: 14, 24, 34 (3 numbers). Total 6.

distractors.E: allowed using the same card twice (and odd numbers)

questions.stem:
The temperature was recorded during one day:
6 am: 13 °C | 9 am: 15 °C | 12 pm: 22 °C | 3 pm: 24 °C | 6 pm: 17 °C
Which statements are correct?
1) The biggest rise was between 9 am and 12 pm.
2) At 3 pm it was more than double the 6 am temperature.
3) The drop from 3 pm to 6 pm was the same as the rise from 9 am to 12 pm.
questions.explanation: Rises: +2, +7, +2, then −7. 1) Biggest rise is +7 (9 am–12 pm) ✓. 2) Double 13 is 26, and 24 < 26 ✗. 3) Drop 24 → 17 is 7, rise 15 → 22 is 7 ✓.

distractors.A: missed that a drop and a rise can be equal

questions.skill: Division with remainder in context, mixed units
questions.stem: Mei has a ribbon 5 m long. Each bow uses 35 cm of ribbon. She makes as many complete bows as she can. How many bows does she make, and how much ribbon is left over?
questions.explanation: 5 m = 500 cm. 35 × 14 = 490, and 35 × 15 = 525 is too much. So 14 complete bows, and 500 − 490 = 10 cm left over.

distractors.B: mixed the remainder from 5000 ÷ 35 with 14 bows
distractors.C: rounded up – there isn't enough ribbon for a 15th bow
distractors.E: converted to mm and rounded up

questions.skill: Area vs perimeter when a corner is removed
questions.stem:
A rectangle is 10 cm by 8 cm. A 3 cm by 3 cm square is cut off one corner, leaving an L-shape. Which statements are correct?
1) The L-shape has a smaller perimeter than the rectangle.
2) The L-shape has an area of 71 cm².
3) The L-shape has a perimeter of 36 cm.
questions.explanation: Area: 80 − 9 = 71 cm² ✓. Perimeter: the two new inside edges (3 cm and 3 cm) replace the two 3 cm pieces that were removed, so the perimeter stays 2 × (10 + 8) = 36 cm ✓. So statement 1 is false.

distractors.C: thought less area means less perimeter
distractors.A: same idea, and didn't check the area
distractors.E: didn't notice 1 and 3 contradict each other

questions.stem: A fish tank is 50 cm long, 40 cm wide and 30 cm high. It is half full of water. How many more litres of water are needed to fill it?
questions.explanation: Full volume: 50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³. 1000 cm³ = 1 L, so it holds 60 L. Half is already full, so 30 L more are needed.

distractors.E: forgot to convert cm³ to litres

questions.stem: 3 apples and 2 pears cost $2.60. 1 apple and 2 pears cost $1.80. How much does ONE pear cost?
questions.explanation: Both orders have 2 pears. The first has 2 more apples and costs $0.80 more, so 1 apple = $0.40. Then 1 apple + 2 pears = $1.80 → 2 pears = $1.40 → 1 pear = $0.70.

questions.skill: Angles on a straight line, vertically opposite angles
questions.stem: Two straight lines cross each other, making four angles. One of the angles is 3 times as big as another one of the angles. What is the size of the LARGEST angle?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles are equal, so the two different angles must be next to each other on a straight line: they add to 180°. Small + 3 × small = 4 smalls = 180°, so small = 45° and large = 135°.

questions.stem: A plane leaves Perth at 11:50 pm and the flight takes 4 hours 25 minutes. Sydney time is 3 hours ahead of Perth time. What is the time in Sydney when the plane lands?
questions.explanation: 11:50 pm + 4 h 25 min = 4:15 am (Perth time). Sydney is 3 hours ahead: 4:15 am + 3 h = 7:15 am.

distractors.B: subtracted the 3 hours instead of adding
distractors.C: it is the next morning, so am

questions.skill: Largest and smallest numbers from digits
questions.stem: Using each of the digits 0, 3, 5 and 8 exactly once, Max makes the largest possible 4-digit number and the smallest possible 4-digit number. What is the difference between them?
questions.explanation: Largest: 8530. Smallest: a 4-digit number can't start with 0, so it is 3058. 8530 − 3058 = 5472.

distractors.A: used 0358, which is not a 4-digit number

questions.stem: Ella spent 1/4 of her money on a book. Then she spent $6 on lunch. Then she spent half of what was left on a game. She had $15 left. How much money did she start with?
questions.explanation: Work backwards: before the game she had $15 × 2 = $30. Before lunch: $30 + $6 = $36. $36 is the 3/4 left after the book, so 1/4 is $12 and she started with $48.

distractors.C: added the $6 at the wrong step
distractors.E: undid the steps in the wrong order

questions.stem: Which of these is the heaviest?
questions.explanation: Change all to grams: 2300 − 450 = 1850 g; 1750 g; 1800 g; 1820 g; 3680 ÷ 2 = 1840 g. The heaviest is 2.3 kg − 450 g.

distractors.D: 1840 g, close but less than 1850 g

questions.stem: Matchsticks are used to make 2 rows of squares. Pattern 1 is a 2 × 1 block of squares, pattern 2 is a 2 × 2 block, pattern 3 is a 2 × 3 block, and so on. How many matchsticks are needed for pattern 12?
questions.explanation: Pattern n has 3 rows of n horizontal sticks (3n) and n + 1 columns of 2 vertical sticks (2n + 2). Total 5n + 2. For n = 12: 60 + 2 = 62. Check: pattern 1 uses 7 sticks ✓.

distractors.B: forgot the 2 sticks at the start

questions.stem: A rectangle is 12 cm long and 8 cm wide. A 3 cm by 2 cm rectangle is cut out from the middle of one of the long sides, making a notch 2 cm deep. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
questions.explanation: The original perimeter is 2 × (12 + 8) = 40 cm. Cutting the notch removes 3 cm of edge but adds 3 cm (the bottom of the notch) plus two 2 cm sides. So the perimeter grows by 4 cm: 44 cm.

distractors.A: forgot the two new sides of the notch
distractors.C: added the notch width as well
distractors.D: added all four sides of the small rectangle

questions.stem: A jug holds 1.2 L of water. Sam pours out 3 glasses of 180 mL each, then adds 250 mL. How much water is in the jug now?
questions.explanation: 1.2 L = 1200 mL. Pouring out 3 × 180 = 540 mL leaves 660 mL. Adding 250 mL gives 910 mL.

distractors.A: forgot to pour out the glasses

questions.stem: This net is folded to make a cube. Which face is opposite face 2?
questions.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 260 110' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='20' text-anchor='middle'><g fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='2'><rect x='5' y='5' width='50' height='50'/><rect x='55' y='5' width='50' height='50'/><rect x='105' y='5' width='50' height='50'/><rect x='105' y='55' width='50' height='50'/><rect x='155' y='55' width='50' height='50'/><rect x='205' y='55' width='50' height='50'/></g><g fill='currentColor'><text x='30' y='37'>1</text><text x='80' y='37'>2</text><text x='130' y='37'>3</text><text x='130' y='87'>4</text><text x='180' y='87'>5</text><text x='230' y='87'>6</text></g></svg>
questions.explanation: In a straight run of three squares, the two end squares are opposite: 1 is opposite 3, and 4 is opposite 6. That leaves 2 and 5 as the last pair, so 5 is opposite 2. (Faces that touch in the net can never be opposite.)

distractors.A: 1 touches 2 in the net, so it can't be opposite
distractors.C: 4 shares a corner with 2 – check where it folds

questions.stem: Ari, Bea and Cy have $60 altogether. Ari has $8 more than Bea. Cy has twice as much as Bea. How much does Cy have?
questions.explanation: Draw bars: Bea = 1 bar, Ari = 1 bar + $8, Cy = 2 bars. 4 bars + $8 = $60, so 4 bars = $52, 1 bar = $13. Cy = 2 × 13 = $26. Check: 13 + 21 + 26 = 60 ✓

questions.skill: Lowest common multiple plus a remainder
questions.stem: A bag has more than 100 sweets. When they are shared equally between 6 children there is 1 left over. The same happens when they are shared between 8 children, and between 9 children. What is the smallest number of sweets the bag could have?
questions.explanation: The number is 1 more than a common multiple of 6, 8 and 9. The lowest common multiple is 72. Multiples: 72, 144, 216... Add 1: 73 (too small, not over 100), 145 ✓.

questions.stem: On a grid, point P is at (2, 3). P is reflected in the vertical line x = 5, and then moved 3 units down. Where does P end up?
questions.explanation: P is 3 units left of the line x = 5, so its reflection is 3 units right of it: x = 8, y stays 3 → (8, 3). Moving 3 down: (8, 0).

questions.stem:
A cuboid 4 cubes long, 3 cubes wide and 2 cubes high is built from small cubes. The outside of the cuboid is painted. Which statements are correct?
1) Every small cube has at least one painted face.
2) Exactly 4 small cubes have paint on just one face.
3) More small cubes have 2 painted faces than have 3 painted faces.
questions.explanation: It is only 2 cubes high, so every cube is on the top or bottom: no hidden middle (1 ✓). One-face cubes are the middle of the top and bottom faces: 2 + 2 = 4 (2 ✓). The 8 corners have 3 faces; the other 12 cubes on the edges have 2, and 12 > 8 (3 ✓).

distractors.B: assumed there must be hidden unpainted cubes
distractors.C: thought corners (3 faces) outnumber edge cubes
distractors.D: assumed a middle cube is hidden

questions.skill: Repeating structure, position in a pattern
questions.stem: The numbers 1, 2, 3, ... are written in 5 columns (1 to 5) in a zigzag. Row 1 goes left to right: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Row 2 goes right to left: 6 is in column 5, 7 in column 4, ... 10 in column 1. Row 3 goes left to right again, and so on. In which column is the number 79?
questions.explanation: Each row has 5 numbers. 75 ends row 15. Row 16 is an even row, so it goes right to left: 76 in column 5, 77 in column 4, 78 in column 3, 79 in column 2.

distractors.D: forgot that even rows go backwards
distractors.E: thought the row starts at column 5 and went the wrong way

questions.skill: Fraction of a remainder, working backwards
questions.stem: Zoe spent 1/3 of her money on a book. Then she spent 1/4 of the money she had LEFT on lunch. She now has $27. How much money did she start with?
questions.explanation: Work backwards. After lunch she kept 3/4 of what was left: 3/4 = $27, so 1/4 = $9 and before lunch she had $36. That $36 was 2/3 of her money: 1/3 = $18, so she started with $54.

distractors.A: stopped at the money before lunch
distractors.D: took 1/3 and 1/4 of the ORIGINAL amount

questions.skill: Probability with linked amounts (trial and improvement)
questions.stem: A bag has red, blue and green counters. There are twice as many blue as red, and 3 more green than blue. The chance of picking a green counter is 1/2. How many counters are in the bag?
questions.explanation: Try values for red. Red 1: blue 2, green 5, total 8 (5 is not half). Red 2: blue 4, green 7, total 13 ✗. Red 3: blue 6, green 9, total 18 – green is 9 out of 18 = 1/2 ✓.

questions.skill: Perimeter of parts from perimeter of whole
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 48 cm. It is cut into 3 identical rectangles, side by side. What is the perimeter of ONE rectangle?
questions.explanation: Square side = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm. Each rectangle is 12 cm long and 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cm wide. Perimeter = 12 + 4 + 12 + 4 = 32 cm.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 identical triangles by lines from its centre to each corner. Two triangles that are next to each other are shaded. What is the smallest number of extra triangles that must be shaded so the hexagon looks the same after a turn of one-third of a full turn?
questions.explanation: A third of a turn moves each triangle 2 places round. If triangles 1 and 2 are shaded, then 3 and 4 must be, and then 5 and 6. All six must be shaded: 4 extra. (2 extra would only give symmetry for a half turn.)

distractors.A: that gives symmetry for a HALF turn, not a third
distractors.D: shading must come in pairs here
distractors.E: the shape changes after a third of a turn

questions.skill: Rounding: the range a rounded number came from
questions.stem: A whole number rounds to 3500 when rounded to the nearest hundred. The same number rounds to 3000 when rounded to the nearest thousand. How many different whole numbers could it be?
questions.explanation: Nearest hundred is 3500 → the number is from 3450 to 3549. Nearest thousand is 3000 → the number is 3499 or less (3500 rounds up to 4000). So it is from 3450 to 3499: that is 3499 − 3450 + 1 = 50 numbers.

distractors.D: counted 3450 to 3549 and forgot an end

questions.stem: A rectangle is divided into a grid of 2 rows and 3 columns of equal squares. How many rectangles of any size (including squares) can be found in the grid?

questions.skill: Rates: a clock that runs fast
questions.stem: A clock gains 4 minutes every hour (it shows 64 minutes for every real hour). It is set to the correct time at 7:00 am. What is the REAL time when the clock first shows 7:00 pm?
questions.explanation: In 11 real hours, the clock moves 11 × 64 = 704 minutes = 11 h 44 min, so it shows 6:44 pm at real 6:00 pm. It needs 16 more clock-minutes. 64 clock-min = 60 real min, so 16 clock-min = 15 real min. Real time: 6:15 pm.

distractors.E: took 48 off and added an hour
